chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya and Hammad ibn Isa and Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn al-Mughira from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while we were in Medina: 'I performed an Umrah in Rajab, and I intend to perform Hajj, so should I bring the offering (Hady) with me, or perform Umrah alone (Ifrad), or combine them (Tamattu')?' He said, 'In all of them is merit, and all are good.' I said, 'Which of these is superior?' He said, 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'For every month, perform an Umrah of Tamattu', for by God it is superior.' Then he said, 'The people of Mecca say that his Umrah was 'Iraqi and his Hajj was Meccan, and they are lying. Is he not bound by his Hajj, not leaving until he completes it?'

key_terms.تَمَتُّعٌ: Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)
key_terms.عِرَاقِيَّةٌ: Iraqi (referring to the type of Umrah performed by the Prophet)
key_terms.مَكِّيَّةٌ: Meccan (referring to the type of Hajj performed by the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Ifrad, Tamattu', and Qiran in Shia jurisprudence, and which is considered superior?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the permissibility of all three Hajj forms while highlighting the superior merit of performing Umrah in Rajab, a practice rooted in Imam Ali’s teachings. It further clarifies the theological distinction between the Prophet’s unified pilgrimage and the Meccans' claim of separate rituals, emphasizing the continuity of the Hajj rites. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet's Sunnah as interpreted through the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly regarding the sanctity of Rajab and the integrity of Hajj rituals.
